result.name: arrivals
result.description: A source: work arriving from the world into a queue, at a rate per hour.
discipline: a source transition has no inputs, so diagnose measures it as a demand knob (more demand ranks negative when losses are the objective)
rates are per hour everywhere in sim; sim_calibrate learns this one from inter-arrival gaps

ports.name: queue
ports.description: where arrivals land; attach to a service's queue

result.name: bounded-queue
result.description: A queue subnet (go-pflow metamodel/queue.go): items and free slots are complementary places, so a positive capacity is a structural P-invariant. Capacity 0 makes it unbounded (enqueue becomes a source).

ports.name: depth
ports.description: the queue length, for read arcs

result.name: datastore
result.description: A capacity-bounded store — the database shape. Writers append records from a source place; the capacity is the disk.
discipline: consumers that only look should use read arcs against the store, not consuming arcs — a query is not a delete
the capacity is a post-firing bound the firing rule enforces; when the store is full, writes refuse rather than silently dropping

ports.name: source
ports.description: records waiting to be written; attach to the producer

ports.name: store
ports.description: the stored records; point read arcs here

result.name: decision
result.description: An operator decision: a budget pool spent through a dormant (rate 0) transition into a target place. Dormant to scenarios; fired only by choice.
discipline: dormant by a rate of 0, the engine's true zero, so plain scenarios are untouched and the decision layer is invisible until an operator spends
the budget is conserved, so every spend is priced against the alternatives

ports.name: target
ports.description: what the spend buys; attach to a staff pool, a spare shelf, a capacity place

params.name: yield
params.description: units minted into the target per spend

result.name: hazard
result.description: Abandonment racing the service: each waiting item independently gives up at a patience rate, into a lost sink.
discipline: the queue arc stays kinetic: each waiting item abandons independently, so loss = patience x mean queue length — which is what staffing moves
the lost sink is fed by a bare hazard, which is exactly what makes diagnose classify it as loss
sim_calibrate cannot learn a hazard racing an instant pickup from completion gaps alone (its observed gap reflects the queue's total drain); declare this rate from knowledge of the world

ports.name: queue
ports.description: the queue being abandoned; attach to the service's queue

ports.name: lost
ports.description: the loss sink; attach to share one loss ledger

result.name: inventory
result.description: A reorder-point stock loop: when stock falls below the reorder point, an order goes out; delivery replenishes in batches after a lead time.
discipline: the reorder trigger is an inhibitor arc (blocks at >= reorder_point), so the threshold is structural — reachability and verify can see it, and it costs nothing at runtime
an inhibitor arc on on_order (weight 1) stops double-ordering while a delivery is in flight
deliveries arrive as a batch (arc weight), which is what makes van/slot contention visible; per-unit trickle would hide it

ports.name: stock
ports.description: the stock being managed; consumers draw from it

params.name: reorder_point
params.description: reorder when stock falls below this

result.name: mailbox
result.description: An asynchronous buffer between a producer and a reader — the email/message-queue shape. Messages land in an inbox; a single reader drains it.
discipline: delivery is kinetic (each message travels independently); reading is non-kinetic (one reader does not read faster because the inbox is fuller) — the same prerequisite-not-accelerant rule as a service pickup
an unbounded inbox is a genuine modeling statement: nothing pushes back on the producer; add a capacity if the real system drops or blocks

ports.name: outbox
ports.description: where messages are sent from; attach to the producer's output place

ports.name: handled
ports.description: messages dealt with; attach to feed downstream work

params.name: read_per_hour
params.description: messages the reader handles per hour

result.name: producer-consumer
result.description: Producer-consumer with a bounded buffer (go-pflow templates).

result.name: queue
result.description: A queueing system: arrivals, a waiting queue, servers and completion (go-pflow templates).

result.name: resource-pool
result.description: A fixed-capacity acquire/release pool (go-pflow metamodel ResourcePool): available + in_use is conserved.

result.name: seir
result.description: SEIR epidemic: Susceptible → Exposed → Infected → Recovered (go-pflow templates).

result.name: service
result.description: A staffed service: a pool of servers picks work from a queue, holds a server while working, releases it on completion into a served sink.
discipline: the queue->pickup arc is non-kinetic at rate 720: a free server notices waiting work in seconds, and a prerequisite is not an accelerant — without this, service speed scales with queue length and staffing questions have no answer
the pool is held across the pickup/finish pair, so headcount is observably binding; seized-and-released-in-one-firing makes staffing irrelevant
the served sink is fed by the pool-releasing transition, which is exactly what makes diagnose classify it as success
sim_calibrate never overwrites the pickup's rate (declared >= 100 marks it): its observed gap is the queue wait, not the pickup

ports.name: queue
ports.description: the work waiting; attach to an arrivals queue

ports.name: served
ports.description: the success sink; attach to share one outcome across services

params.name: per_hour
params.description: completions per busy server per hour

result.name: sir
result.description: SIR epidemic: Susceptible → Infected → Recovered (go-pflow templates).

result.name: workflow
result.description: A sequential workflow of `stages` steps, Stage0 → … → Stage<stages> (go-pflow templates).

notes: I -> svc_pickup is non-kinetic in service; the pflow.xyz document has no kinetic flag, so the ODE treats it as mass-action

predicates.name: hasMember
predicates.comment: a collection's member; membership is an edge so the collection's own content id never changes when something joins it

predicates.name: broader
predicates.comment: the subject is a narrower case of the object, as a human classified it

predicates.name: narrower
predicates.comment: the inverse reading of broader; never stored, link broader the other way round

predicates.name: related
predicates.comment: an associative link, read the same in either direction

predicates.name: closeMatch
predicates.comment: a human claim that two models represent the same kind of system; never a proof (isomorphicTo is the proved form)

predicates.name: cites
predicates.comment: the subject draws on the object without being derived from it (derivation is lineage)

predicates.name: about
predicates.comment: a report, dataset or table concerning a model, collection, binding or system

predicates.name: from
predicates.comment: a binding's source model; recorded by sim_bind with the binding itself

predicates.name: to
predicates.comment: a binding's target model; recorded by sim_bind with the binding itself

predicates.name: feeds
predicates.comment: one model's output port is bound to the other's input; recorded by sim_bind

predicates.name: produced
predicates.comment: the result a prompt actually returned

predicates.name: supersededBy
predicates.comment: old version → its replacement, recorded by store.supersede (sim_supersede_model)

predicates.name: isomorphicTo
predicates.comment: the same net up to renaming (coloured-net-v1); stored with the smaller id as subject

predicates.name: subnetOf
predicates.comment: the subject embeds injectively in the object, arcs induced (induced-incidence-v1)

predicates.name: migratedFrom
predicates.comment: a taxonomic edge on a successor model → the edge on a superseded version it was carried forward from; recorded only by store.accept_migration

predicates.name: preservesInvariant
predicates.comment: the subject embeds in the object along a map under which every P-invariant of the object pulls back (invariant-pullback-v1)

predicates.name: refines
predicates.comment: every firing sequence of the subject, silent transitions dropped, is one of the object (id-simulation-v1)
